music.title: Mozart — Piano Sonata in C major K.545, first movement opening
music.arrangement: Source melody/accompaniment in order, with a two-bar G-to-C HolyMind cadence, softer dynamics and a slower bounded performance. Not the complete sonata.
music.piano_samples: Alexander Holm / Salamander Grand Piano, CC BY 3.0

behavior.scroll: Trusted scroll advances an ordered, time-scheduled score at 78–100 BPM. Speed changes tempo gently, at most two BPM per beat. No random chords, note skipping or rapid scroll-event triggering.
behavior.pause: Stops scheduling new beats after the current scheduled beat. Sounding notes retain natural decays and room resonance. Next scroll resumes at the next score beat.
behavior.reverse: Upward scrolling also continues the chronological score, not reversed audio or backwards note order. The approved directional electric current still responds to direction.
behavior.sections: Section changes affect warmth, room and dynamics without resetting the musical cursor. Action keys use the current harmonic context; while the score moves they become restrained aligned accents.
behavior.release: Eleven six-second recorded piano keys; per-note overlapping releases, approximately 2.45 s for melody and 1.70 s accompaniment, plus a 2.8 s room response. Foreground cue tails no longer forcibly preempt at 65 ms.
behavior.resources: Maximum 36 score voices, six foreground cue tails, a 48-phrase cache and one AudioContext. Paused score scheduler stops; sources clean up.
behavior.controls: Existing sound preference independently controls the score/action keys; always-on visual motion is unchanged. Mute/background stop audio intentionally; a fresh gesture resumes after interruption without old scroll intent.
behavior.preserved: Original Quiet Current ambient/scroll graph, fourteen Electric v12 brain sounds, original artwork, mobile-only brain-first layout, all original controls and pinned assembly.

offline_audio.normalization: None; production graph, 0.48 master gain and shared compressor

limitations.preview_method: OfflineAudioContext renders of the production piano score/room, not microphone recordings.
